channel.title: Arabic Edition on Aljareeda
channel.description: Recent content in Arabic Edition on Aljareeda

item.title: Morocco Is Embedding Judges in Its Embassies to Speed Up Diaspora Cases
item.description: Morocco will station liaison judges in its diplomatic missions to follow cross-border civil, family and criminal cases. Also in issue 7513: a customs reorganisation, 13,470 hectares of tribal land fixed in law, and a new dam in Safi.

item.title: Morocco Appoints Fatima Zahra Mansouri as Head of Government
item.description: Issue 7548 names Fatima Zahra Mansouri Head of Government, sets a 30-day online mortgage-release process for state housing aid, approves €585.53 million in foreign loans, and clears a new Tanger Med container terminal deal.

item.title: Morocco Extends Free Land Registration in 29 Zones
item.description: Morocco’s Official Gazette issue 7547 extends free land registration in 29 zones, lets governors cut local-debt enforcement costs, approves the Marchica lagoon plan, and clears a cancer-care software merger with binding conditions.

item.title: Morocco's Top Court Strikes Down Parts of Its New Adoul Law
item.description: Gazette issue 7520: the Constitutional Court rules on the adoul law, an online platform for debt-enforcement payments, 18 foreign degrees recognized, and a national biodiversity warning.

item.title: Morocco Fast-Tracks Land Seizures for New Casablanca–Rabat Highway and High-Speed Rail Expansion
item.description: This issue of the Official Gazette clears land for a new Casablanca-Rabat highway and expanding high-speed rail lines, reshapes the Bouregreg riverbanks in Rabat-Salé, and cancels two unused aquaculture concessions near Dakhla while licensing a new one near Sidi Ifni.

item.title: Morocco's Child Labor Fell 80% Since 1999 — But 101,000 Kids Still Work, State Council Warns
item.description: A landmark advisory-council report on child labor, a new Marrakech-Agadir-Essaouira high-speed rail declaration, land seized to widen the Kenitra-Marrakech line, and two MPs stripped of their seats for political defection — from Morocco’s Official Gazette issue №7541.

item.title: Morocco Ends Closed-Door Contracting for Mosque and Waqf Projects
item.description: A new decree forces Morocco’s religious endowment administration to open its construction and supply contracts to competitive, publicly advertised bidding for the first time, with mandatory online publication, set-asides for small businesses, and a complaint channel for bidders.

item.title: Morocco Caps E-Scooters at 25 km/h and Hands Vehicle Paperwork to a New Safety Agency
item.description: This issue of Morocco’s Official Gazette rewrites road-safety rules for e-scooters and drivers, shifts vehicle registration to a new agency, and clears land for a dam, two drinking-water projects, a port expansion and a highway widening.

item.title: Morocco Overhauls the Legal Profession, Makes Impersonating a Lawyer a Prison Offense
item.description: A new law rewrites the rules for who can practice law in Morocco and criminalizes impersonating a lawyer, alongside a judicial appointments fix and a Settat water project.

item.title: Six Moroccan Lawmakers Quit in Ten Days — Constitutional Court Declares Seats Vacant
item.description: Six Moroccan MPs resigned in ten days, the Constitutional Court moved fast to fill the gap, foreign-trained doctors got new equivalency routes, and three companies were licensed to farm shrimp, oysters and fish along the coast.

item.title: Morocco Turns Its Port Authority Into a Company — and Locks In $1.2B a Year for Regions
item.description: Ports of Morocco SA is born, regions get a 12-billion-dirham annual floor, Bank Al-Maghrib gets bank-resolution powers, and a new real-estate law shakes up how land gets developed — all from this week’s Official Gazette.

item.title: Morocco Rewrites Drug Pricing Rules — and Clears Land for High-Speed Rail and OCP's New Phosphate Line
item.description: Morocco rewrites its drug-pricing formula, clears land for high-speed rail and OCP’s phosphate corridor, pipes water to Taounate, launches a Youth Pass, and formalizes tribal land boundaries — all from this week’s Official Gazette.

item.title: Morocco's Top Court Blocks Government From Picking the Judiciary's Own Senior Staff
item.description: Morocco’s Constitutional Court blocks the executive from appointing senior officials inside the judiciary’s own governing body, while the state launches four new AI and digital-transformation institutes under the ‘Jazari’ brand.

item.title: Morocco's Own Watchdog Says Street Violence Is Up 29% — And Nobody's Punished for It
item.description: This issue’s real news: a hard-numbers state report on rising public disorder, more land seized for the Marrakech high-speed rail extension, RAM’s new pilot-and-mechanic training arm, and extended tariff breaks on wheat and meat.

item.title: Morocco Greenlights Land for New High-Speed Rail Line to Marrakech
item.description: This week’s Official Gazette: land cleared for the Kénitra–Marrakech high-speed line, a nationwide university expansion, new refurbished-medical-device rules, and 25,000+ hectares of tribal land formally recognized.

item.title: Morocco Plans Digital Overhaul of Its Islamic Notary System
item.description: Morocco’s Economic, Social and Environmental Council wants blockchain security, AI tools, and gender-parity rules built into a rewrite of the law governing the country’s roughly 3,100 Adouls — the traditional notaries who certify marriage, divorce, inheritance, and will documents that Moroccans abroad frequently need.
